rationale: Section IX.B synthesizes cocoa beverages, dark chocolate and mood. Anxiety stratification and metabolic endpoints in Martin 2009 are separate from the measured state anxiety reported by Scholey. Use the original trials as separate families and the review as a citation trail.
Olive oil supplies background fatty-acid and nitric oxide comparisons. The article does not report extra-virgin olive oil against constipation.
Coffee appears in antioxidant or cardiovascular contexts. The mental fatigue comparison uses cocoa beverages with differing flavanol content and does not isolate brewed coffee.
Olive oil is a background comparator for fatty acids and vascular compounds. The cocoa studies do not test cold-pressed olive oil and anxiety.
Cranberry juice cocktail appears in a food composition table. Depression and mood observations involve chocolate, without a dried cranberry comparison.
Cocoa and chocolate are the review exposures. There is no ground sage intervention or patient fall-frequency outcome.
Grapes and grape juice appear in polyphenol or antioxidant comparisons. The measured or discussed anxiety pertains to chocolate or cocoa.
The reported fatigue comparison concerns cocoa-flavanol mixtures and the paper does not test fresh sage.
Green tea is discussed for antioxidant properties and food chemistry. The acute mental-fatigue comparison tests cocoa beverages, without a brewed green tea comparison.
Broccoli is a general analogy for whole-food effects and cruciferous vegetables appear in dietary background. The review provides no steamed-broccoli fall comparison.
Sodium benzoate is an isolated cinnamon metabolite. DJ-1 and other protein measures supply mechanistic context without a ground-cinnamon exposure or passive rigidity measure.
Rest tremor appears as Parkinson background and Figure labels identify experimental illustrations. The paper does not study raw fig or measure rest tremor.
Isolated caffeine affects measured rodent wakefulness. Arousal and activity endpoints do not establish a brewed coffee effect on clinical fatigue.
The isolated-caffeine rodent wakefulness experiment did not compare poached chicken or measure fatigue severity.
